safetyTips.title: Use Metered Tuk-Tuks or PickMe / Uber
safetyTips.summary: Always agree on a meter or use ride-hailing apps to avoid inflated tourist fares.
safetyTips.details: In Colombo and major cities, insist on using the meter ('Taxi Meter'). In rural areas (e.g. Ella, Sigiriya), agree on the price BEFORE getting in. Using local apps like PickMe or Uber gives you transparent pricing and trackable GPS trips.

safetyTips.title: Solo Female Night Travel Caution
safetyTips.summary: Avoid walking alone in poorly lit or unpopulated areas after 9:00 PM.
safetyTips.details: While Sri Lanka is generally friendly and safe, solo female travelers should avoid secluded beaches, dark alleys, or unlit rural roads late at night. Arrange pre-booked tuk-tuks or hotel transport when returning late from dinner or beach parties.

safetyTips.title: Beware of 'Friendly Local' Gem & Herbal Scams
safetyTips.summary: Be cautious if a friendly stranger invites you to a 'special one-day gem exhibition' or spice garden.
safetyTips.details: A common scam in Kandy and Galle involves touts offering to show you a 'rare gem sale' or 'free government herbal garden' where prices are inflated by 10x. Kindly decline ('No thank you') and purchase only from licensed establishments.

safetyTips.title: Train Door Safety & Scenic Routes
safetyTips.summary: Do not hang dangerously out of open train doors on the Kandy-Ella railway line.
safetyTips.details: The famous Kandy to Ella train is stunning, but hanging out of open doors for photos has led to severe accidents against tunnels, rocks, and trees. Always hold handles securely inside the carriage.

safetyTips.title: Tap Water & Hygiene Guidelines
safetyTips.summary: Drink filtered or bottled water only; avoid raw unpeeled roadside fruit.
safetyTips.details: Tap water in Sri Lanka is not recommended for direct drinking. Stick to sealed bottled water or filtered water provided by hotels. Eat hot, freshly cooked food from busy local eateries.

safetyTips.title: Respect Religious Symbols & Buddha Statues
safetyTips.summary: Never pose with your back turned to a Buddha statue, and do not display visible Buddha tattoos.
safetyTips.details: Taking photos facing away from a Buddha statue (selfies with your back turned) is strictly illegal and offensive. Ensure shoulders and knees are covered when entering temples (e.g., Temple of the Tooth, Dambulla). Buddha tattoos must be covered in public.

safetyTips.title: Ocean Currents & Beach Safety Flags
safetyTips.summary: Heed red warning flags on beaches (e.g., Mirissa, Hikkaduwa, Arugam Bay).
safetyTips.details: Sri Lanka's coastline has strong rip currents, especially during monsoon transitions. Never swim alone when a red flag is displayed on the beach. Ask local lifeguards or surf instructors before swimming.

safetyTips.title: SIM Card & Emergency Connectivity
safetyTips.summary: Get a local tourist eSIM/SIM (Dialog or SLT Mobitel) upon arrival at BIA Airport.
safetyTips.details: Dialog and Mobitel have coverage across 95% of the island including remote hill country. Having active data ensures you can access Google Maps, translation apps, PickMe, and emergency calls anytime.

safetyTips.title: Wildlife & Elephant Encounters on Roads
safetyTips.summary: Do not feed wild elephants or step out of vehicles in jungle corridors (e.g., Habarana / Yala).
safetyTips.details: Wild elephants frequently cross roads near Sigiriya, Habarana, and Udawalawe. Stay inside your vehicle, do not use high beams or loud horns, and never attempt to approach them on foot.
